  The upgrade needs three code changes before it is safe. Each one can ship and run on 6.5.12 first. Without them, two features break in ways the test suite can't catch. A fourth problem, the export failure, is caught by existing tests.
  
  I ran this myself because no subagent tool was available here. The working repo is unchanged (`git status` is clean). All experiments ran in `/tmp/sk7exp/{app,appB,appC}`. They used their own Redis server on port 6390 with a separate db per run, their own PostgreSQL databases `sk7exp_*` (set through `DATABASE_URL`), and each copy's own `storage/` and `tmp/`. All logs are in `/tmp/sk7exp/logs/` and probe scripts in `/tmp/sk7exp/scripts/`. The Redis server is stopped and the databases are dropped; the logs remain.

  All copies use Ruby 3.3.6, Rails 7.0.8.7 and a local Redis server 7.0.15.
  
  | Copy | Sidekiq | connection_pool | redis-client | redis gem | How it was made |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | A (`app`) | 7.3.9 | **3.0.2** | 0.31.0 | 4.8.1 | `bundle lock --update sidekiq` (adding `--conservative` gives the same result) |
  | B (`appB`) | 7.3.9 | 2.5.5 | 0.31.0 | 4.8.1 | Gemfile also pins `connection_pool 2.5.5`, only in this copy |
  | C (`appC`) | 6.5.12 | 2.5.5 | — | 4.8.1 | Unchanged baseline |
  
  ## Required changes
  
  ### R1. `ExportJob` arguments with symbol keys now raise an error
  - **Code:** `app/models/notebook.rb:26`, `ExportJob.perform_async(export.id, { format: "markdown" })`.
  - **Why:** Sidekiq 7 turns on strict argument checking by default. A job argument that isn't plain JSON raises `ArgumentError` when the job is queued. On 6.5 it only logged a warning.
  - **Tested:** `bin/rails test` fails with 3 errors in `ExportsControllerTest` in both A and B (`logs/test_app.log`, `logs/test_appB.log`).
  - **Fix:** pass `{ "format" => "markdown" }`. This works on 6.5.12 too, and the job already reads `options.fetch("format")`.
  
  ### R2. Digest requests fail because of the `BigDecimal` argument (tests can't catch this)
  - **Code:** `app/models/user.rb:41`, `DigestJob.perform_later(self, requested_at, reading_completion)`.
  - **Why:** Active Job 7.0 passes a `BigDecimal` through to Sidekiq unchanged, and Sidekiq 7 rejects it when the job is queued.
  - **Why tests miss it:** the test environment uses Active Job's `:test` adapter.
  - **Tested:** in `logs/probe_appB_full.log`, `request_digest` raised `ArgumentError: Job arguments to DigestJob must be native JSON types, but 0.0 is a BigDecimal`. The rescue then removes the reservation, so every digest request fails with an error. On 6.5 (`logs/probe_appC.log`) the same call only warns.
  - **Fix:** pass `reading_completion.to_s`. The job already receives the value as a decimal string today, so `DigestJob` and `DigestMailer` see no change. This works on 6.5.12.
  - **Docs:** update `ARCHITECTURE.md` (around lines 159–171 and 201), which describes the `BigDecimal` and the warning.
  
  ### R3. Duplicate digest requests are no longer blocked
  - **Code:** `app/models/user.rb:38`, `if Sidekiq.redis { |redis| redis.sadd(key, id) }`.
  - **Why:** Sidekiq 7 talks to Redis through redis-client, whose `sadd` returns `1` or `0`. In Ruby, `0` counts as true, so the "already requested" branch never runs.
  - **Tested:**
    - On 7.3.9 the call returns `sadd new=1 dup=0`; on 6.5 it returns `new=true dup=false` (probe logs).
    - Once R2 is fixed this would send duplicate digests. The test `DigestsControllerTest#...one digest per UTC day` already fails in A and B ("on its way" instead of "already requested").
  - **Fix:** `Sidekiq.redis { |r| r.call("SADD", key, id) } == 1`. I checked that this returns `1` then `0` on both versions (`logs/portable_appB.log`, `logs/portable_appC.log`). It also removes the redis-rb deprecation warning on 6.5. Don't use `sadd?`, because Sidekiq 7's Redis adapter doesn't provide it.
  
  ### R4. A Redis outage during export no longer cleans up (tests can't catch this)
  - **Code:** `app/models/notebook.rb:28`, `rescue Redis::BaseError`.
  - **Why:** Sidekiq 7 raises `RedisClient::CannotConnectError`, which is not a `Redis::BaseError`. The `redis` gem is still installed, so the code loads without error, but the rescue never matches. A failed queue then leaves a queued `Export` with no job behind it.
  - **Tested:** with Redis unreachable, 7.3.9 raised `RedisClient::CannotConnectError is_a Redis::BaseError=false`, while 6.5 raised `Redis::CannotConnectError ... =true` (`logs/probe_down_*.log`).
  - **Why tests miss it:** the related test in `digests_controller_test.rb:50` stubs `Redis::CannotConnectError` itself, so it passes either way.
  - **Fix that also works on 6.5:** rescue both classes. `RedisClient` isn't defined on 6.5, so build the list with a guard:
    ```ruby
    REDIS_ERRORS = [Redis::BaseError, (RedisClient::Error if defined?(RedisClient))].compact
    ...
    rescue *REDIS_ERRORS
    ```
  - **Tests:** add a model test that stubs `ExportJob.perform_async` to raise each error class, and have it assert that the export is removed.
  
  ### R5. `connection_pool` jumps to 3.0.2 unless you pin it
  - **Why:** Sidekiq 7.3.9 accepts `connection_pool >= 2.3.0`, so Bundler resolves 3.0.2, a major version. This happens even with `--conservative`.
  - **Tested:** A (3.0.2) and B (2.5.5) gave identical results: same test failures, probes and boot.
  - **Not established:** that 3.x is safe for every Rails 7.0 path. The app has no Redis cache store and doesn't use connection_pool directly. It is used only through Sidekiq and redis-client.
  - **Recommendation:** pin `connection_pool` to `"~> 2.5"` for this upgrade and handle 3.x as its own change, unless you deliberately accept it. The project rules say to keep dependency versions unless the task authorizes changing them.
  
  ## Prep changes that work on 6.5.12
  R1–R4 can all ship and run on 6.5.12 before the gem bump; R1–R3 were checked there directly. To check the prep release on 6.5 before bumping, add `Sidekiq.strict_args!` (6.5 provides it, as `logs/portable_appC.log` confirms). Run the app with the Sidekiq adapter and confirm that requesting a digest and an export no longer log the "do not serialize to JSON safely" warning.
  
  ## Behavior changes worth noting (optional)
  - **Default concurrency drops from 10 to 5 threads per process.** The app has no `config/sidekiq.yml` and no Sidekiq initializer, so this applies. Set `-c 10` (or a `sidekiq.yml`) if you want the old throughput. This is from upstream notes; I didn't measure it. The database `pool` (`RAILS_MAX_THREADS`, 5) matches 5 threads; going back to 10 would also need a larger pool.
  - **Sidekiq's internal and client Redis pools changed.** The run logged `size=>10, pool_name=>"internal"` (Sidekiq 7's own pool). Check how many Redis connections you're allowed.
  - **Leave strict argument checking on.** `Sidekiq.strict_args!(false)` would hide R1 and R2, but don't use it as the fix.
  - **New Web UI and metrics.** Not mounted in `config/routes.rb`, so nothing to do.
  - **Separate Redis gems.** Action Cable keeps using the `redis` 4.8.1 gem (`config/cable.yml`), while Sidekiq no longer uses it. Keep `gem "redis"` in the Gemfile.
  
  ## Redis server version
  Sidekiq 7 requires Redis 6.2 or newer (upstream requirement; I didn't test an older server). The local and orb server is 7.0.15. **Production's Redis version is unknown.** The repo has no verified deployment, so check it with `redis-cli INFO server` before rolling out.
  
  ## Mixed versions, queued work and rollback
  **Tested** against shared Redis and PostgreSQL (`logs/worker_appC-appB.log`, `logs/worker_appB-appC.log`):
  - **Forward:** 6.5 queued an `ExportJob` with symbol keys, a `DigestJob` with a `BigDecimal`, a delayed `NoteReminderJob`, and a job that always fails. A 7.3.9 worker processed all of them: the export completed with its file, the digest finished, the scheduled reminder moved to the queue and ran, and the failing job went to the retry set with its retry data intact.
  - **Rollback:** 7.3.9 queued the same jobs (with prep-safe arguments) and a 6.5 worker processed them the same way.

  1. Deploy R1–R4 on 6.5.12.
  2. Bump the web and worker processes. They can run mixed for a while: the old code queues jobs only through a 6.5 client, which only warns.
  3. Rollback to 6.5 is safe as long as R1–R4 stay in place. Rolling back the code changes while keeping 7.3.9 brings R1–R4 back.

  - A retry entry created by a 6.5 worker and then picked up by a 7.3.9 worker. I only tested jobs queued by 6.5 and retried by 7.3.9; this is inferred safe from the shared JSON format.
  - Web UI and process heartbeat keys while both versions run side by side.
  - The dead set across versions.
  
  ## Checks still proposed
  1. Apply R1–R5 in a copy on 7.3.9 and rerun `bin/rails test`. The 4 current failures should go away.
  2. Add the R4 rescue test, and an integration test that runs `request_digest` through the real `:sidekiq` adapter against an isolated Redis. That test would catch R2 and R3.
  3. Run `bin/rails test:system` and `bin/rails zeitwerk:check` on 7.3.9. Neither has been run.
  4. Check production Redis is 6.2 or newer, and the connection limit.
  5. Run an end-to-end development smoke test with `bundle exec sidekiq` on 7.3.9 and `bin/citation-provider` covering citation enrichment, including `retry_on` and the hand-off to Sidekiq's own retries. Citation jobs weren't exercised.
  6. Read the official Sidekiq 7.0 upgrade notes (`docs/7.0-Upgrade.md`) and the 7.x changelog for removed APIs. The app uses none I could find, but I didn't read those docs in this session; the API and default-change claims above come from my knowledge of Sidekiq, not from fetched docs.

- **Code:** `app/models/user.rb:41`, `DigestJob.perform_later(self, requested_at, reading_completion)`.
- **Why:** Active Job 7.0 passes a `BigDecimal` through to Sidekiq unchanged, and Sidekiq 7 rejects it when the job is queued.
- **Why tests miss it:** the test environment uses Active Job's `:test` adapter.
- **Tested:** in `logs/probe_appB_full.log`, `request_digest` raised `ArgumentError: Job arguments to DigestJob must be native JSON types, but 0.0 is a BigDecimal`. The rescue then removes the reservation, so every digest request fails with an error. On 6.5 (`logs/probe_appC.log`) the same call only warns.
- **Fix:** pass `reading_completion.to_s`. The job already receives the value as a decimal string today, so `DigestJob` and `DigestMailer` see no change. This works on 6.5.12.
- **Docs:** update `ARCHITECTURE.md` (around lines 159–171 and 201), which describes the `BigDecimal` and the warning.

### R3. Duplicate digest requests are no longer blocked
- **Code:** `app/models/user.rb:38`, `if Sidekiq.redis { |redis| redis.sadd(key, id) }`.
- **Why:** Sidekiq 7 talks to Redis through redis-client, whose `sadd` returns `1` or `0`. In Ruby, `0` counts as true, so the "already requested" branch never runs.
- **Tested:**
  - On 7.3.9 the call returns `sadd new=1 dup=0`; on 6.5 it returns `new=true dup=false` (probe logs).
  - Once R2 is fixed this would send duplicate digests. The test `DigestsControllerTest#...one digest per UTC day` already fails in A and B ("on its way" instead of "already requested").
- **Fix:** `Sidekiq.redis { |r| r.call("SADD", key, id) } == 1`. I checked that this returns `1` then `0` on both versions (`logs/portable_appB.log`, `logs/portable_appC.log`). It also removes the redis-rb deprecation warning on 6.5. Don't use `sadd?`, because Sidekiq 7's Redis adapter doesn't provide it.

### R4. A Redis outage during export no longer cleans up (tests can't catch this)
- **Code:** `app/models/notebook.rb:28`, `rescue Redis::BaseError`.
- **Why:** Sidekiq 7 raises `RedisClient::CannotConnectError`, which is not a `Redis::BaseError`. The `redis` gem is still installed, so the code loads without error, but the rescue never matches. A failed queue then leaves a queued `Export` with no job behind it.
- **Tested:** with Redis unreachable, 7.3.9 raised `RedisClient::CannotConnectError is_a Redis::BaseError=false`, while 6.5 raised `Redis::CannotConnectError ... =true` (`logs/probe_down_*.log`).
- **Why tests miss it:** the related test in `digests_controller_test.rb:50` stubs `Redis::CannotConnectError` itself, so it passes either way.
- **Fix that also works on 6.5:** rescue both classes. `RedisClient` isn't defined on 6.5, so build the list with a guard:
  ```ruby
  REDIS_ERRORS = [Redis::BaseError, (RedisClient::Error if defined?(RedisClient))].compact
  ...
  rescue *REDIS_ERRORS
  ```
- **Tests:** add a model test that stubs `ExportJob.perform_async` to raise each error class, and have it assert that the export is removed.

### R5. `connection_pool` jumps to 3.0.2 unless you pin it
- **Why:** Sidekiq 7.3.9 accepts `connection_pool >= 2.3.0`, so Bundler resolves 3.0.2, a major version. This happens even with `--conservative`.
- **Tested:** A (3.0.2) and B (2.5.5) gave identical results: same test failures, probes and boot.
- **Not established:** that 3.x is safe for every Rails 7.0 path. The app has no Redis cache store and doesn't use connection_pool directly. It is used only through Sidekiq and redis-client.
- **Recommendation:** pin `connection_pool` to `"~> 2.5"` for this upgrade and handle 3.x as its own change, unless you deliberately accept it. The project rules say to keep dependency versions unless the task authorizes changing them.

## Mixed versions, queued work and rollback
**Tested** against shared Redis and PostgreSQL (`logs/worker_appC-appB.log`, `logs/worker_appB-appC.log`):
- **Forward:** 6.5 queued an `ExportJob` with symbol keys, a `DigestJob` with a `BigDecimal`, a delayed `NoteReminderJob`, and a job that always fails. A 7.3.9 worker processed all of them: the export completed with its file, the digest finished, the scheduled reminder moved to the queue and ran, and the failing job went to the retry set with its retry data intact.
- **Rollback:** 7.3.9 queued the same jobs (with prep-safe arguments) and a 6.5 worker processed them the same way.

Why stored jobs are safe: Redis already holds them as JSON, so their arguments are plain strings by the time they're read. Strict checking only runs when a job is queued. Jobs waiting from before the upgrade, including scheduled reminders and retries with a `BigDecimal` or symbol keys, therefore run on 7.x.

1. Deploy R1–R4 on 6.5.12.

Mixed-version processes don't affect digest reservations (one Redis set per day), because both versions now use `call("SADD") == 1`.
